# Overview

`Edge_Score1D()` performs miRNA gene interaction (MGI) enrichment
analysis by testing whether a pathway's MGIs are located unexpectedly
toward one end of a ranked MGI list. Unlike `Edge_Score2D()`,
`Edge_Topology()`, and `Edge_Network()`, `Edge_Score1D()` does not
implement its own permutation loop and has no `iter` or `seed` argument.
It is a GSEA style test, delegated entirely to
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("clusterProfiler")`'s `GSEA()`, which performs its
own permutation based significance testing internally.

This vignette uses the same toy BLCA example data as the package's main
Quick Start vignette. See `vignette("miREA")` for a description of that
data and for running all nine methods together through `miREA()`.

# Required inputs

* `pathway`, a three column data frame with columns `pathway`, `miRNA`,
  and `gene`.
* `mir_DEdata`, a four column data frame with columns `miRNA`,
  `log2FoldChange`, `stat`, and `padj`.
* `gene_DEdata`, a four column data frame with columns `gene`,
  `log2FoldChange`, `stat`, and `padj`.
* `mir_mat` and `gene_mat`, raw expression matrices with samples as
  columns, used to score each MGI.
* `scoreFun`, the transform applied to the correlation and differential
  expression values when building the ranked MGI score, for example
  `"rank"`.
* `background_MGI`, a two column data frame with columns `miRNA` and
  `gene`, or `NULL` to use the bundled default (see `vignette("miREA")`,
  Step 1, for details on `background_MGI`).

```{r load-data}
library(miREA)
data(toy_pathway)
data(toy_mir_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_mat)
data(toy_mir_mat)
data(background_MGI)
```

# Run Edge-Score1D

```{r prepare-input}
input_data <- getAllInputData(
    methods = "Edge_Score1D",
    pathway = toy_pathway,
    mir_DEdata = toy_mir_DEdata,
    gene_DEdata = toy_gene_DEdata,
    background_MGI = background_MGI,
    gene_mat = toy_gene_mat,
    mir_mat = toy_mir_mat,
    scoreFun = "rank"
)
```

`input_data$data$Edge_Score1D` holds the ranked MGI list, built by
`getAllInputData()` from correlating `toy_gene_mat` and `toy_mir_mat`
expression and transforming the result with `scoreFun`.
`input_data$pathway$Edge` holds the pathway MGI sets, derived from
`toy_pathway`'s genes through `background_MGI`.

```{r run-edge-score1d}
res <- Edge_Score1D(
    MGIList = input_data$data$Edge_Score1D,
    pathway = input_data$pathway$Edge,
    pvalueType = "neg",
    pvalueCutoff = 1,
    minSize = 2,
    maxSize = 5000
)
head(res)
```

# Run through miREA()

`Edge_Score1D()` can also be run through the `miREA()` wrapper, which is
useful when you want its result alongside other methods' results in a
single `miREAResult` object (see `vignette("miREA")`, Step 2, for the
multi-method case). `Edge_Score1D()` itself has no `background` argument,
but `miREA()` still requires one for the `Edge` target, since
`Edge_ORA()`/`Edge_Score2D()`/`Edge_Topology()` share that target and do
use it. For a single target, `background` can be a plain character
vector instead of a named list.

```{r run-through-miREA}
background <- unique(paste0(background_MGI$miRNA, ":", background_MGI$gene))
result <- miREA(
    methods = "Edge_Score1D",
    input_data = input_data,
    background = background,
    pvalueCutoff = 1,
    minSize = 2,
    maxSize = 5000
)
head(result$result$Edge_Score1D)
```
